The fifth period delves deeper into JavaScript programming, covering advanced topics and best practices. The sixth period applies full-stack development concepts to a real-world project, using Python and JavaScript. The seventh period focuses on frontend development, covering HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in-depth. The eighth period introduces back-end development with Node.js and Express, building on previous courses. The ninth period covers full-stack development with JavaScript, including Node.js and Express. The final period introduces version control and collaboration with Git and GitHub, essential for web development.

This learning path starts with a foundational understanding of project management life cycle (EDX2192) and builds on existing knowledge with project management foundations (EDX3229). The path then introduces Agile project management principles and practices (EDX3248) and gradually increases in complexity with advanced project management concepts (EDX3326). The emphasis is on strategic thinking and decision-making (EDX3342), followed by practical application of project delivery methods and contracts (EDX1489). The path continues to build on existing knowledge, introducing project delivery methods and contracts, and emphasizes risk management and contract management. Finally, the path integrates Agile delivery principles and practices, and provides opportunities for practical application and hands-on experience.

| 10 | COU3697 | Industrial Biotechnology | Coursera | Introduction to industrial biotechnology and its applications |

**How the path fits together**

This learning path starts with a foundational course in biology and programming (COU149), followed by a course that builds on prior knowledge in biology and genetics (COU2930). The next course introduces genomics and genetics (COU2929), and then delves into genomics and data science (COU5783). The path continues with a course on finding mutations in DNA and proteins (COU1249), which emphasizes concepts over memorization in bioinformatics and genomics. The next course focuses on Python programming for genomic data science (COU5134), incorporating visual and interactive learning. The path then builds on prior knowledge in biology and genetics (COU3367), followed by a course on genetics and evolution (COU3709). The final courses in the path cover bioinformatics and genomics (COU318) and industrial biotechnology (COU3697). This learning path provides a comprehensive and structured approach to molecular biology and genetics, with a focus on building on prior knowledge and skills.
